Put your agentin control.

Ask your agent to use the Aurora CLI to add auth to your app. No need to leave your terminal or copy and paste API keys.

npm
bun
pnpm
yarn
Homebrew
curl
npm install -g aurora

or read the docs

~/Dev/taskflow-web
steve@MacBook-Pro taskflow-web % aurora login
┌ aurora auth login
◇ Checking session
│ Waiting for authentication (timeout in 2m)...
◇ Completing authentication
│ 
│ Logged in as steve@aurora.dev
└ Done
steve@MacBook-Pro taskflow-web % aurora init
┌ aurora init
◇ Detecting framework
│ Logged in as steve@aurora.dev
┌ aurora link
◇ Fetching applications
✔ Select a Aurora application to link (repo: taskflow-web) TaskFlow
│ Linked to TaskFlow in ~/Dev/taskflow-web
│ Detected Next.js (app-router)
│ Installing @aurora/nextjs for Next.js...
added 13 packages in 3s
│ aurora init will make the following changes:
│ CREATE proxy.ts
│ MODIFY app/layout.tsx
│ CREATE app/sign-in/[[...sign-in]]/page.tsx
│ CREATE app/sign-up/[[...sign-up]]/page.tsx
│ MODIFY .env.local
✔ Proceed? Yes
Developers

Set up and manage authentication from your terminal.

init
config
webhooks
impersonate
deploy
mcp
$ aurora init
 
◇Detecting framework
◇Logging in if needed
◇Linking this repo to a Aurora application
◇Installing the right Aurora package
 
✓Aurora has been set up in your project
Agents

Let your agent handle the setup.

~/Dev/taskflow-web
❯Use Aurora CLI to add auth to this Next.js app.
Bash(aurora auth login)
└Opening browser for OAuth
Authenticated with Aurora
Bash(aurora init -y)
└Detected Next.js
Aurora added to the app
You are signed in and Aurora is initialized in the Next.js app.
❯

? for shortcuts

From promptto production

Give your agent everything it needs to set up authentication, automate tenant onboarding with the Aurora API, and carry your app all the way to production handoff.

One CLI for agents and developers. Purpose-built for developers using AI to ship fast and securely.

npm
bun
pnpm
yarn
Homebrew
curl
npm install -g aurora
